claims.text: AddResilienceHandler (Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience) on an IHttpClientBuilder takes a handler name and a delegate configuring a ResiliencePipelineBuilder<HttpResponseMessage>; every request sent by that HttpClient runs through the pipeline, and its response or exception comes back through it.

claims.text: Strategies in a resilience pipeline execute in the order they are configured; the first added is the outermost: a request meets it first on the way out and its outcome last on the way back, so it sees each inner execution and its outcome.
claims.source_hint: Microsoft Learn: core/resilience index, 'Build a resilience pipeline' (order is important); Polly docs: Resilience pipelines

claims.text: Polly's timeout strategy (AddTimeout with a TimeSpan) cancels an execution that exceeds the timeout and throws TimeoutRejectedException, not System.TimeoutException.

claims.text: AddStandardResilienceHandler chains five strategies, outermost to innermost: rate limiter, total timeout (30 s), retry (max 3 retries, exponential backoff, jitter), circuit breaker, attempt timeout (10 s); these are default options that overloads let you customize.
claims.source_hint: Microsoft Learn: core/resilience/http-resilience, 'Standard resilience handler defaults' table

claims.text: By default the standard resilience handler retries requests for all HTTP methods, including POST; DisableFor or DisableForUnsafeHttpMethods turns retries off for chosen methods.
claims.source_hint: Microsoft Learn: core/resilience/http-resilience, 'Disable retries for a given list of HTTP methods'

claims.text: With 3 retries, one execution makes up to 4 calls (one initial attempt plus three retries); so each RefundSender attempt through the standard handler could reach the gateway up to 4 times.
claims.source_hint: Microsoft Learn: core/resilience index, ExecuteAsync example ('executed four times'); standard handler defaults table

claims.text: In the standard handler the total timeout, added before (outside) the retry, limits the request including retry attempts; the attempt timeout, added after (inside) it, limits each attempt.
claims.source_hint: Microsoft Learn: core/resilience/http-resilience, 'Standard resilience handler defaults' (Total timeout, Attempt timeout rows)

claims.text: Program.cs comment lines 89-97 @ stage-3: no retry strategy, unlike AddStandardResilienceHandler, because RefundSender already tries each refund again on a later round and retries in both places would multiply the calls.
The standard resilience handler fits a client whose caller does not retry and whose requests are safe to repeat; when the caller already retries, a custom pipeline without retry fits better.
Retries in two layers multiply gateway calls during an outage; the refund Idempotency-Key prevents a second refund but not the extra load on a recovering gateway.
